lesson_success_checks: Identify a hazard and who could be harmed/how. Explain one suitable control and who to tell. Read common sign shapes with symbols and words. Keep one short individual risk-and-control card and a clear report.

Accepted business, supervisor/preparer/checker roles, paper order, editions, tier packs and cover-plan structure. Only Week 2 newly authored.

Friday 15 January P1, pair, forty minutes. Scene hazards, common sign shapes/words, who/how to report and one short risk/control card per learner. No real employer, product, regulator or place. Weeks 3–6 one per return. Pause for Downloaded.

routes.Supported: Choose B spill or C stack. Use the scene, two hazard choices, word bank, report frame and model A. Give hazard, who/how harmed, one control, who to tell and a short message. Book, pointing, voice, aid, typing or exact scribe valid.
routes.Standard: Choose B or C. Explain the hazard and possible harm, select one suitable control and who arranges it, then rehearse a clear report. Link a sign type to its meaning. Complete your own short risk-and-control card.
routes.Stretch: Compare a warning sign with a control that deals with the hazard. Explain what risk remains and how a supervisor could check the control. Evaluate D without calling it risk-free. Use the same short individual card; extra writing optional.

business.description: An invented small business prepares simple paper packs for customers. It has a supervisor, a preparer and a checker. It has no name, real employer, location or contact details. This is classroom simulation only.
business.order: Prepare two paper packs. Each pack needs one large card and one paper strip. Put the items beside each other. Check both packs against this order. Tell the checker when they are ready.
business.roles: The preparer arranges the materials. The checker reads the order and checks each pack. Agree roles, then swap after resetting the materials. An adult can take the other role if preferred.
business.limits: Use ready-cut paper only. No scissors, staplers, machines, food, money, customer data, live orders or deliveries. Accuracy, communication and support matter; speed is not assessed.

cases.title: The walking route
cases.hazard: An empty box is in the walking route.
cases.who_harm: A worker using the route could trip over the box and fall.
cases.immediate: Keep clear of the route and tell the supervisor. Warn someone approaching if you can do so safely.
cases.control: The supervisor arranges safe removal of the box and checks the route is clear.
cases.report: There is a box in the walkway by the packing table. Someone could trip. I am keeping clear. Please arrange for the route to be cleared and checked.

cases.title: Beside the packing table
cases.hazard: Water is spilled on the floor beside the table.
cases.who_harm: A worker walking there could slip and fall.
cases.immediate: Stay clear and report the spill to the supervisor. Do not step into it or clean an unknown spill yourself.
cases.control: The supervisor arranges suitable cleaning and drying, keeps people clear and checks the floor before reuse.
cases.report: There is a spill beside the packing table. Someone could slip. I am keeping clear. Please arrange for it to be dealt with and checked.

cases.title: The high shelf
cases.hazard: Paper packs lean over the edge of a high shelf.
cases.who_harm: A worker below could be struck if packs fall; reaching or climbing could add a fall risk.
cases.immediate: Keep away from below the stack and tell the supervisor. Do not climb, reach up or try to catch falling packs.
cases.control: The supervisor arranges safe restacking at a suitable height, away from edges, and checks storage.
cases.report: Packs are leaning at the edge of the high shelf. They could fall on someone. I am keeping clear. Please arrange for the stack to be made secure.

cases.title: Controls in place
cases.hazard: No deliberate hazard is shown in this comparison scene. It is not proof every risk is absent.
cases.who_harm: Clear routes, a dry floor and stable reachable packs reduce the pictured trip, slip and falling-pack risks.
cases.immediate: Keep these controls in place and report any change. Ask about anything that remains unclear.
cases.control: Keep access clear, floor dry and packs secure; the supervisor checks changes and storage.
cases.report: The pictured route is clear and the floor looks dry. I would keep these controls and ask about anything I cannot check from the picture.

signs.label: Warning
signs.action: Notice the hazard, keep clear and check the instructions.

signs.label: Prohibition
signs.action: Do not enter the marked area; ask the supervisor if unsure.

signs.label: Mandatory
signs.action: Follow the specified protection instruction before the relevant task; ask if unclear.

signs.label: Safe condition
signs.meaning: Shows a safe route or help.
signs.action: Use the marked information and tell an adult if help is needed.

worked_examples_status: All worked examples, workplace scenes, workers and events are invented and declared. Simplified sign diagram is authored for teaching shapes/messages, not installation. No real employer, product, regulator, place, incident or workplace inspection.
private_help_route: Use a trusted adult or the school’s help route. Point to HELP, write or ask privately. If one adult is busy, seek another through the route. Pass, pause and supported return available. No personal accident account or disclosure requested.
typed_and_scribed_routes: Evidence Sheet page 2 blank short card for every tier. Book, voice, aid, typing or exact scribe valid. Read back/correct; normal access distinct from answer prompts. Save with code/work reference and share privately.
adaptations: Cognition and Learning: one scene/field at a time, reduced choices, model and frames. Communication and Interaction: wait, rehearse, use aid, read/write exact words. SEMH: predictable private turns, pass/pause/return. Sensory and Physical: large scenes, verbal description, seated role and no colour-only meaning. EAL: plan in any language. 1 Point to place/instruction; 2 ask a short question; 3 rephrase; 4 scaffold/choice; 5 model first step only then return task.
worked_example_and_fade: A: box is hazard, trip/fall is possible harm. Report to supervisor and stay clear. Supervisor arranges safe removal/check. Ask if “box” or “fall” names the hazard; key box. Keep model, scene and words; fade answer cues for B/C only.

main_hinge.claim: A warning alerts; the hazard still needs suitable control and checking.

parallel_hinge.claim: Pause and ask about an unclear instruction rather than guess.

assessment: Keep one individual risk-and-control card with scene/hazard, who/how harmed, one suitable control and responsible role, report message, immediate action and a check/unknown. Evidence Sheet page 2 blank typed alternative, page 3 staff record. Book/usual aid default. A selected or dictated message is valid; record access separately from answer prompts.
judgement: Judge a plausible hazard/harm link, a relevant control and a clear report to the supervisor/adult. Accept an explained alternative visible in a scene. Risk is not a synonym for the hazard itself. No numeric matrix or real inspection is required. D shows useful controls but cannot prove all risks absent. Do not infer job readiness, a real incident response or compliance from classroom work.

evidence.description: Individual short risk-and-control card and report, with hazard/place, who/how, control/role, immediate action, check/unknown, access and NS/reply.

where_this_leads: This helps me notice a hazard, keep clear and give a useful report before starting or returning to a work task.
colour_blind_safe: Shapes, symbols, words and scene labels carry meaning. Colour is an extra clue, never the sole cue.

asset.description: New generated four-scene 2 by 2 bank, invented/unnamed. Native crops and editable labels.

sign_asset.description: Authored precise shape-and-word teaching diagram. Not installation artwork.

safety_boundary: Learners observe pictures, keep clear and report. They do not remove obstructions, clean unknown spills, climb/reach/catch stacks or operate equipment. In a real concern follow the school/workplace reporting and emergency procedures; adult supervises immediate action. If the first supervisor is unavailable or the hazard remains, use the agreed route to another responsible adult; do not resume simply because a sign was placed.

0–5: retrieve Week 1 safety/help expectation; ask what a worker can do if unsure. 5–9: hazard is something that could cause harm; risk considers how likely and how serious harm could be; control reduces risk. Use A box/route, worker trip/fall, keep clear/report and supervisor-arranged removal/check. 9–13: teach four sign categories with shape, symbol and written meaning. Read the words even when colour is available.

13–19: compare A with D; identify what changed and what cannot be known from a picture. Match sign type/shape/message. A wet-floor warning helps warn but does not remove the spill. Rehearse a report: what, where, possible harm, keep-clear action and request. Adult plays supervisor and acknowledges the concern. 19–23: hinge B: warning alone does not remove the hazard. Parallel A: unclear instruction, pause/ask rather than guess. Re-model and recheck privately.

23–27: use Supported/Standard/Stretch prompt with B spill or C stack. 27–32: each learner makes a short card: hazard and scene, who/how harmed, control and responsible role, report, immediate action and check/unknown. 32–35: each gives a brief report to adult/partner through usual mode; adult may partner privately. Each owns a card; do not copy the adult model as independent evidence.

35–38: privately check one card/report for correct hazard-versus-harm and a control that fits. Keep first try, set one NS and retain reply. 38–40: name who to tell and one safe first action; bank actual card/report. Missing response stays unobserved with a follow-up.

These are invented scenario guides, not learner observations.
Hazard: An empty box is in the walking route. Harm: A worker using the route could trip over the box and fall.
Immediate response: Keep clear of the route and tell the supervisor. Warn someone approaching if you can do so safely.
Control: The supervisor arranges safe removal of the box and checks the route is clear.
Hazard: Water is spilled on the floor beside the table. Harm: A worker walking there could slip and fall.
Immediate response: Stay clear and report the spill to the supervisor. Do not step into it or clean an unknown spill yourself.
Control: The supervisor arranges suitable cleaning and drying, keeps people clear and checks the floor before reuse.

A box is the hazard; trip/fall is possible harm. Report to supervisor, keep clear, safe removal/check arranged by supervisor. If learner confuses cause and harm, point to box then describe what could happen. Do not imply a real route has been cleared.
Paper packs lean over the edge of a high shelf. A worker below could be struck if packs fall; reaching or climbing could add a fall risk.

Keep away from below the stack and tell the supervisor. Do not climb, reach up or try to catch falling packs. The supervisor arranges safe restacking at a suitable height, away from edges, and checks storage.

No deliberate hazard is shown in this comparison scene. It is not proof every risk is absent. Clear routes, a dry floor and stable reachable packs reduce the pictured trip, slip and falling-pack risks.
Keep these controls in place and report any change. Ask about anything that remains unclear. Keep access clear, floor dry and packs secure; the supervisor checks changes and storage.
